entries.prompt: To fasten something firmly so it cannot slip or fall.
entries.why: To secure a thing is to fix it firmly in place, so it holds.

entries.prompt: A sticky substance, such as glue or paste, that holds things together.
entries.why: An adhesive is anything sticky, like glue or paste, that holds things together.

entries.prompt: To tie things tightly together with cord.
entries.why: To bind is to tie things tightly together, as you bind a split handle with cord.

entries.prompt: A straight strip of wood tied on to hold a cracked pole still.
entries.why: A splint is a straight strip of wood, tied on to hold a broken part still while it mends.

entries.prompt: To join cloth with a needle and thread.
entries.hint: It sounds just like so, but it is spelled another way.
entries.why: To sew is to join cloth with a needle and thread.

entries.prompt: Strong and solid, and not easily broken.
entries.hint: Its middle sounds like the ur in fur.
entries.why: Something sturdy is strong and solid, so it does not break easily.

entries.prompt: A paste that sets as hard as stone and joins bricks together.
entries.hint: It starts with a c that sounds like s.
entries.why: Cement is a paste that dries as hard as stone, joining bricks and stones together.

entries.prompt: To make something broken or worn whole again.
entries.hint: It begins with re-, which means again.
entries.why: To repair a thing is to make it whole and working again.

entries.prompt: To close a rip in cloth, loop by loop, with needle and thread.
entries.hint: It ends with the same three letters as catch.
entries.why: A stitch is one loop of thread. To stitch a rip is to close it loop by loop.

entries.prompt: To put up again something that fell down.
entries.why: Re- means again. To rebuild is to build a thing again after it falls.

entries.prompt: To put a new part where a worn-out one was.
entries.why: To replace a part is to take the old one out and put a new one in its place.

entries.prompt: To join two things firmly so they hold together.
entries.hint: There is a quiet t you do not hear.
entries.why: To fasten is to join things firmly, as a buckle fastens a strap.

entries.prompt: To turn a loose bolt until it holds firm.
entries.hint: It has the same igh as night.
entries.why: To tighten is to make a thing tight, so it no longer wobbles.

entries.prompt: To join metal pieces by melting them together with heat.
entries.why: To weld is to heat two pieces of metal until they melt and join as one.

entries.prompt: A short metal pin hammered flat to hold two plates together.
entries.why: A rivet is a metal pin. Its ends are hammered flat so the plates cannot come apart.

entries.prompt: To make something stronger by adding extra support.
entries.hint: In the middle you can hear force.
entries.why: Re- means again: to reinforce is to give a thing more strength with extra support.

entries.prompt: To shine with a wet, sparkling light, as dew does.
entries.hint: There is a quiet t in it.
entries.why: To glisten is to shine with a wet, sparkling light.

entries.prompt: A stick of wax with a wick that burns.
entries.why: A candle is a stick of wax round a wick. The wick burns and the wax melts.

entries.prompt: To shine with a soft light that seems to move.
entries.hint: Two m's sit in the middle.
entries.why: To shimmer is to shine with a soft, wavering light, like moonlight on water.

entries.prompt: To shine so brightly that it is hard to see.
entries.hint: Two z's sit in the middle.
entries.why: To dazzle is to shine so brightly that it almost blinds you.

entries.prompt: To blaze up suddenly with a bright flame.
entries.why: To flare is to blaze up in a sudden, bright flame.

entries.prompt: Very bright and shining.
entries.hint: There are two l's in the middle.
entries.why: Something brilliant shines very brightly.

entries.prompt: A tiny bit of fire that jumps from struck flint.
entries.why: A spark is a tiny bit of fire. Strike flint and steel, and sparks fly.

entries.prompt: Full of light; not dim at all.
entries.hint: The long i sound is spelled igh, as in night.
entries.why: Something bright is full of light.

entries.prompt: A small glowing piece of coal left in a fire.
entries.hint: Its first part sounds like the letter m.
entries.why: An ember is a glowing bit of coal or wood that stays hot after the flames die down.

entries.prompt: To burn unsteadily, flashing on and off.
entries.why: A flame that flickers jumps and dims, then flares again.

entries.prompt: A big, fierce fire that burns brightly.
entries.why: A blaze is a big, bright fire.

entries.prompt: A small, clear flash of light off something shiny.
entries.why: A gleam is a small flash of light, like sun on a polished cup.

entries.prompt: To start a small fire with dry twigs and sticks.
entries.why: To kindle a fire is to start it with small, dry twigs.

entries.prompt: To set something on fire.
entries.hint: Its last part sounds like night.
entries.why: To ignite is to set a thing on fire. The root ign means fire.

entries.prompt: A faint, wavering light, seen far off.
entries.why: A glimmer is a faint light that wavers, like a far-off candle.

entries.prompt: Shining with light or warmth; glowing.
entries.why: Something radiant sends out light or warmth all around it, like the sun.

entries.prompt: To give thirsty plants a long, deep drink.
entries.why: To soak plants is to give them so much water it sinks deep into the soil.

entries.prompt: To wet a cloth or the soil lightly.
entries.hint: It ends with -en, which means to make.
entries.why: To dampen is to make a thing a little wet.

entries.prompt: A long, open box that holds water for animals to drink.
entries.why: A trough is a long, open box of water, where farm animals drink.

entries.prompt: How much water comes down from the clouds on a place.
entries.hint: It is two words joined into one.
entries.why: Rainfall is how much rain falls on a place.

entries.prompt: To scatter small drops of water over something.
entries.why: To sprinkle is to scatter small drops, as rain does.

entries.prompt: A very heavy fall of rain.
entries.hint: Its second part means to tip out.
entries.why: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain that pours down.

entries.prompt: To make something wet all the way through.
entries.why: To drench is to make a thing wet all the way through.

entries.prompt: To soak something so fully it can hold no more water.
entries.hint: It ends like the ate in skate.
entries.why: To saturate a thing is to soak it so fully that it can take in no more water.

entries.prompt: Light rain that falls in very fine drops.
entries.hint: It has two z's, as in fizzle.
entries.why: Drizzle is light rain in very fine drops.

entries.prompt: A thin, slow stream of water.
entries.why: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of water.

entries.prompt: To take away thirst with a drink.
entries.hint: It starts with qu, as in queen.
entries.why: To quench thirst is to drink until you are thirsty no more.

entries.prompt: A short fall of rain.
entries.why: A shower is a short fall of rain.

entries.prompt: To cover dry land with water.
entries.hint: It rhymes with mud, but its middle is spelled with two letters.
entries.why: To flood is to cover land with water.

entries.prompt: A narrow ditch that carries water to the fields.
entries.hint: Two n's sit in the middle.
entries.why: A channel is a narrow ditch that carries water from one place to another.

entries.prompt: To take in water, as a sponge or dry soil does.
entries.why: To absorb is to take in, as dry soil absorbs the rain.

entries.prompt: Tiny drops of water in the air or the soil.
entries.why: Moisture is a little water spread through the air or the soil.

entries.prompt: To turn a key so a door can swing wide.
entries.hint: It starts with un-, which means undo.
entries.why: To unlock is to undo a lock with a key.

entries.prompt: To undo the metal fastener on a belt.
entries.why: To unbuckle is to undo a buckle.

entries.prompt: To spread out a map or a cloth that was creased flat.
entries.why: To unfold is to open out what was folded.

entries.prompt: To pull something out, as a cork from a jar.
entries.hint: It starts with ex-, which means out.
entries.why: To extract is to pull a thing out.

entries.prompt: To raise the catch that keeps a gate shut.
entries.why: To unlatch is to lift the catch, the latch, so a gate can swing.

entries.prompt: To make a gap or a doorway broader.
entries.hint: It ends with -en, which means to make.
entries.why: To widen is to make a thing wider.

entries.prompt: To make a knot or a lid less tight.
entries.why: To loosen is to make a thing less tight.

entries.prompt: To take the paper or cloth off a parcel.
entries.hint: There is a silent w after un-.
entries.why: To unwrap is to take off the wrapping.

entries.prompt: To draw back the metal rod that holds a door shut.
entries.hint: Its last part rhymes with colt.
entries.why: To unbolt is to slide back a bolt, the rod that holds a door shut.

entries.prompt: Left a little bit open, as a door not quite shut.
entries.why: A door that is ajar is open just a little.

entries.prompt: To undo a buckle, clasp or strap.
entries.hint: There is a quiet t after the s.
entries.why: To unfasten is to undo whatever holds a thing shut.

entries.prompt: To let something go so it is free.
entries.why: To release is to let go, so a thing is free.

entries.prompt: To force something apart with a bar or a tool.
entries.why: To pry is to force a thing apart with a bar, as you pry up a stuck lid.

entries.prompt: To break the wax that keeps a letter shut.
entries.why: To unseal is to break the seal, the wax that keeps a letter closed.

entries.prompt: To undo the metal catch on a book or a purse.
entries.why: A clasp is a metal catch. To unclasp is to undo it.

entries.prompt: To knock something loose from where it was stuck.
entries.hint: It starts with dis-, meaning away.
entries.why: To dislodge is to knock a thing loose from where it was stuck fast.

entries.prompt: To start to grow, as a seed pushes up its first green tip.
entries.why: To sprout is to begin to grow, as a seed puts up its first shoot.

entries.prompt: To care for something young as it grows.
entries.why: To nurture is to feed and care for a young thing as it grows.

entries.prompt: To gather in the crops when they are ripe.
entries.why: To harvest is to gather the crops once they have grown and ripened.

entries.prompt: A field of fruit trees.
entries.why: An orchard is a field where fruit trees grow.

entries.prompt: A flower on a fruit tree in spring.
entries.hint: Two s's sit in the middle.
entries.why: A blossom is a flower, most often on a fruit tree.

entries.prompt: To grow ready to eat, as fruit does in the sun.
entries.hint: It ends with -en, which means to become.
entries.why: To ripen is to become ripe, ready to eat.

entries.prompt: A young tree with a thin trunk.
entries.hint: It starts like sap, the juice inside a tree.
entries.why: A sapling is a young tree.

entries.prompt: A tiny young plant, just up from the soil.
entries.why: A seedling is a young plant that has just grown from a seed.

entries.prompt: An arm of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
entries.why: A branch is an arm of a tree, growing out from the trunk.

entries.prompt: Rotted leaves and scraps that feed the soil.
entries.hint: It starts with the same three letters as comb.
entries.why: Compost is rotted leaves and scraps. Dug into the soil, it feeds the plants.

entries.prompt: Rich enough for plants to grow well.
entries.why: Fertile soil is rich, so plants grow well in it.

entries.prompt: To feed something so it grows strong and well.
entries.hint: It begins like the start of nurse.
entries.why: To nourish is to feed a thing so it can grow strong.

entries.prompt: To do well and grow strong.
entries.why: To thrive is to grow strong and do well.

entries.prompt: To grow strongly and well, full of health.
entries.hint: It starts with the letters of flour.
entries.why: To flourish is to grow strongly and well.

entries.prompt: Fully grown, as an adult plant or animal.
entries.why: Something mature is fully grown.

entries.prompt: To dig and tend the land so crops grow.
entries.why: To cultivate land is to dig it, sow it and tend the crops as they grow.
